system.summary: Marked numerical groups represent French words and word parts.

diacritics.note: Superscripts and trailing strokes distinguish numerical groups in the strict transcriptions.

prior_solution.where: Period decipherments in Nationaal Archief, 2.01.08 inv. 248. No. 23 trained the table. The two March test references were sealed separately. Before fitting, the investigator had seen a small view of scan 174 including part of a French page. The January investigator had seen its clear copy.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed this project. AI agents transcribed the documents and performed the tests. Models, from the Codex app logs of 19–20 November 2026: reader A of every cipher panel and of the inventory 204A annotations ran on gpt-6.1-terra; reader B on gpt-6.2-astra; the coordinating agent (which transcribed and sealed the French references) and the agent that fitted the table, froze the plans and scored the tests on gpt-6.2-astra. The 14 November survey that located the letters was made by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent with helper agents.

solution.what: 14 November: my inventory survey (my own working notes, made with a Claude Opus 5.5 agent and helper agents, not in this repository) paged inventory 248 and listed nine Vienna cipher dispatches with period decipherments, and separated the Vienna papers from the Düsseldorf target. Revisited on 19 November.

Two readers transcribed each cipher panel independently before reconciliation: No. 7 at 21:44 and 21:46 UTC, No. 23 at 21:52–21:56, No. 26 at 22:00–22:03 and No. 21 at 22:11–22:14 (file write times in the agents’ logs; reader A gpt-6.1-terra, reader B gpt-6.2-astra). The French references were transcribed separately by the coordinating agent; No. 26 sealed at 22:05:53 UTC and No. 21 at 22:11:41 UTC.

January within-letter test, plan and inputs frozen at 21:49:11 UTC: it matched two of five predictions, both de. Of 1,000 shuffled controls, 226 tied or exceeded that score. The investigator had seen the French reference.

Plan frozen at 22:05:30 UTC. Two monotone dynamic-programming alignments against the period copy for No. 23 agreed on 93 marked group candidates, 53 whole words and 40 fragments; the table and predictions were frozen at 22:07:38 UTC.
The frozen table (22:07:38 UTC) predicted 43 whole tokens for No. 26. 32 matched the French source sealed at 22:05:53 UTC within the registered position window. Best shuffled score 16.

Plan frozen at 22:11:18 UTC, reference sealed at 22:11:41 and predictions frozen at 22:14:48. The same table predicted 61 tokens for No. 21. 48 matched the sealed source within the registered window. Best shuffled score 20. The sole complete word assembled from fragments missed.

Plan and inputs frozen at 22:21:19 UTC. In the separate Düsseldorf comparison only two word placements were testable, below the minimum of eight. The unread companion was left untested. Plan, No. 6 transcription and script in vienna_contribution/dusseldorf/.
After both tests, two readers read the later inventory 204A annotations independently (22:16 and 22:18 UTC) and placed the reported 227 in a Munich dispatch. None of the notes entered the Vienna fit.

validation.notes: This contribution has sparse, position-tolerant word predictions and no continuous token-aligned reading for an n-gram test. The frozen March protocols compare the fixed table against two historical decipherments and 1,000 shuffled tables per letter.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The March table was fitted to No. 23 and its contemporary decipherment in the same archive file.

credits.note: Partial reconstruction and two prospective cross-letter tests of the marked numerical table, with AI agents. All four historical readings predate this work.
French clear copies used for training and comparison.

texts.label: No. 7, 24 January
texts.summary: The period copy discusses General Vincent’s mission and what the French ambassador knew about it.
texts.note: Historical French reference. No. 7 was the separate January within-letter test, which missed. It was not used to fit the March table, no January value entered that table, and it supplies no independent reconstructed reading.

texts.label: No. 23, 21 March
texts.summary: The period copy describes preparations to travel to Holland and reports plans for an Austrian militia.
texts.note: Historical French reference. The project used this letter for fitting; it supplies no independent reconstructed reading.

texts.label: No. 26, 28 March
texts.summary: The period copy reports artillery moved at night and discusses conflicting reports about its destination.
texts.note: Sparse output of the fixed March candidate table, including every slot.

texts.label: No. 21, 14 March
texts.summary: The period copy reports a conversation with Count Stadion and a request for leave.
texts.note: Sparse output of the fixed March candidate table, including every slot.

outcome.notes: The selected predictions use a positional tolerance and count words against historical references. They supply no document-wide read share. Three whole-word candidates matched every opportunity across both held-out letters. Most of the 93 entries remain provisional.
